 Advertisement Madras HC Refuses to Stay OTT Release of Ajay Devgn’s ‘Dhrishyam: The Conclusion’ in Copyright Dispute
 Ravin Yadav 18 November 2026, 9:00 AM IST Madras High Court refuses Rajkumar Theatres' plea to restrain the OTT exploitation of Ajay Devgn's Dhrishyam: The Conclusion in a copyright dispute. - Rajkumar Theatres Pvt. Ltd. v. Wide Angle Creations and 6 Others
 Advertisement The Madras High Court has refused to restrain the OTT release and further exploitation of Ajay Devgn and Tabu-starrer Drishyam: The Conclusion , dismissing an interim injunction application filed by Rajkumar Theatres Private Limited over the Hindi remake rights of the Drishyam franchise. 
 Justice P.B. Balaji passed the order on November 13, 2026, holding that the applicant had failed to establish a prima facie right to prevent the original Malayalam film's producers and director from assigning adaptation rights to other parties. 
 Advertisement Background 
 Rajkumar Theatres approached the High Court claiming a 50% share in the Hindi remake rights of the Malayalam film Drishyam and its sequels. The dispute arose from agreements executed between Wide Angle Creations, the original Malayalam film's producers and director, and subsequent production companies. 
 The company argued that its contractual rights covered Hindi adaptations and sequels, and alleged that the production of Drishyam: The Conclusion infringed those rights. 
 The respondents disputed the claim, maintaining that the Hindi film was an independent adaptation based on rights separately acquired by Panorama Studios. 
 Examining four agreements executed between 2013 and 2025, the Court found that Rajkumar Theatres had not established ownership of the entire copyright or a subsisting right to prevent the original copyright holders from assigning adaptation rights. 
 The Court also noted that the film's censor certificate identified it as Drishyam: The Conclusion , although promotional material had earlier referred to it as Drishyam 3. The applicant had also failed to specifically demonstrate how the released film infringed its claimed sequel rights. 
 Advertisement Justice Balaji further considered that an earlier application under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, seeking substantially the same interim protection against the same respondents, had already been dismissed on merits on October 1, 2026. 
 The Court observed, 
 "I do not see any merit in this line of argument as well." It held that the applicant could not renew the same interim injunction request in a civil suit after allowing the earlier adverse order to attain finality. 
 Finding that Rajkumar Theatres had failed to establish entitlement to interim protection, both on the merits of its claimed rights and in view of the earlier proceedings, the High Court dismissed the application. 
 The Court clarified that refusing interim protection would not automatically deny the applicant relief in the main suit. 
 Accordingly, the Original Application was dismissed without costs.
